hypothesis: For an explicitly opted-in reasoning workload, withholding the onset chunk plus the next two locally generated answer chunks and routing with the separately trained k2 probe preserves the previously observed Reasoning-zh fixed-budget gain while preventing a user from hearing a local answer that is later discarded for expert relay.

scope.disabled: default live traffic and automatic task-family inference

policy.local_decision: release all buffered chunks in original order, then stream normally
policy.expert_decision: discard all buffered chunks before any client emission, then use the existing lossless TTS expert relay
policy.short_answer_rule: if end_of_turn arrives before k2, release the buffered local answer and do not escalate
policy.interruption_rule: discard the pending local buffer and return to listening; do not relay stale content

acceptance_gates: Reasoning-zh delivered accuracy delta at the exact 30% budget is at least +0.030
No local audio or text is emitted before the k2 decision
The local path releases all three buffered chunks exactly once and in order
The expert path releases no buffered local chunk
A pre-k2 end_of_turn cannot strand or silently drop a short local answer
An interruption clears buffered content and prevents stale delivery
The default/deployed onset gate and artifact remain unchanged
decision_rule: Any failed gate rejects P36. Passing authorizes an opt-in implementation candidate only; it does not authorize default activation. The latency cost is reported as two post-onset answer-chunk intervals and is not hidden inside the expert latency measurement.
mechanical_amendment: Code-path inspection established that X_k2 is captured after two answer chunks following the onset chunk. Therefore three generated chunks, not two, must be buffered. This correction was made before publishing the validation result and changes no score, threshold, population, or acceptance gate.
